questions.lead: The near side of the Moon and its far side look very different, and scientists have argued about why for decades. A new study compared rocks collected from both hemispheres.
questions.prompt: Which mission first brought back samples from the Moon's far side?

questions.lead: In the team's model the Moon's early magma ocean cooled evenly at first. Things changed once the Moon settled into an orbit that kept the same hemisphere facing our planet, when the two were much closer together.
questions.prompt: What does the study say heated the near side of the Moon more than the far side?
options: Heat from a giant collision with another body
Heat from radioactive decay in the crust

sources.excerpt: In auto racing, Formula 1 announces a new grand prix in Kigali, Rwanda, to run for at least 10 years starting in the early 2030s with a new track.
This would be the first F1 grand prix in Africa since South Africa in 1993.
This Vincent van Gogh Painting Has Not Been Seen in Public for Over 60 Years. It Is Now Poised to Set a Record at an Upcoming Auction
The Dutch Post-Impressionist painted "Chestnut Trees in Blossom" during the highly productive yet tragic final months of his life.
It is heading to auction as part of a "legendary" private collection which also includes works from Cézanne and Renoir
A New Contender for the World's Oldest Shipwreck Has Been Discovered Off the Coast of Turkey. Its Ancient Cargo Is a 'Time Capsule' From 4,700 Years Ago
The ship was likely transporting huge jars of olive oil or wine across the Mediterranean when it sank to the seafloor.
A major opportunity to investigate this mystery arrived in 2024, when Chang'e-6 became the first mission to return samples from the Moon's far side.
Their findings suggest that uneven heating from Earth's gravitational pull drove enormous flows of ancient magma, creating the dramatically different lunar landscapes we see today.
In contrast, the far side is dominated by ancient, heavily cratered highlands, with a much thicker crust and relatively few volcanic plains.
